title: Book Three · Chapter 108: Twenty and a Half
story:
On Saturday morning, Ronan takes the forty-one yuan to the table.

He puts twenty in one envelope for Leo. He puts twenty in another for himself. One yuan is left.

Mum comes over with her work money box. She changes his one-yuan coin for two half-yuan coins.

“The same money,” she says. “Two smaller pieces.”

Ronan puts one half-yuan coin in each envelope. Now each holds twenty and a half yuan.

He writes the amount on both. Then he checks it against Leo's letter.

The ten good books are in two groups of five. Leo's railway and garden books have L inside. His three other books have B. Ronan's five all have B marks.

Each group goes into one cloth bag.

Ronan keeps his own bag and envelope at home. He carries Leo's to the grandmother's near the old market.

She has received Leo's note. She asks Ronan to come in and puts a clean cloth on the table.

They count the money together. Twenty yuan and one half-yuan coin. Twenty and a half in all.

Then she counts the five books and looks at the list.

“He wants the railway one again?”

“He chose it.”

She smiles. “I thought he might.”

Ronan shows her Leo's letter. She reads the request about the bag and money, then folds it carefully.

“I can keep them for him. Here, with his other things.”

She puts the envelope inside the bag and gives it a place in her cupboard. The bag, five books, and twenty and a half yuan belong to Leo now. She is keeping them for him.

On Ronan's copy of the list, she writes her name beside the amount and the five books.

He thanks her and takes the list home.

Mum is serving a customer near the window. Ronan waits in the yard and counts his own five books again.

He puts the half-yuan coin beside the twenty. He started with twenty yuan and three books. Now he has twenty and a half yuan, five books, and one bag. This is his share of the whole sale.

He thinks of the seventeen books they sold and the three that came back. He thinks of the table, the torn pages, and Anna outside the library.

Then he puts his envelope away.

The shared cash has all been divided. No saleable books or bags remain in the joint pile. Only the two damaged books and the old card are waiting for Monday.

Ronan takes his football from beside the blue bike. Kai is meeting him in the park after lunch, and he has time to walk there.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

half-yuan coin＝半元硬币；amount＝金额；cupboard＝柜子；share＝分得的一份。

## 理解问题

1. 四十一元怎样分给两人？一元换成两个半元后，总金额有没有改变？
2. Leo的五本书、布袋和钱由谁实际保管？这是Ronan私自决定的吗？

## 读句子

**Now each holds twenty and a half yuan.**

拆开看：Now / each holds / twenty and a half yuan.

现在／每个信封各装着／二十元五角。
